title: Collaborative Knowledge Extraction and Integration for Graph Domain Incremental Learning

problem.claim: Graph Domain Incremental Learning must acquire knowledge from a continuous stream of graph domains while mitigating catastrophic forgetting.

gap.claim: Prompt-based techniques struggle to adapt to GDIL, while low-rank adaptation based on a shared classification layer can cause knowledge confusion; transferable knowledge is primarily concentrated in the representation layer.

contributions.claim: COOKER mines inter-domain relationships and uncovers domain-agnostic representations for graph domain incremental learning.

COOKER uses domain-specific LoRA modules and classifiers to capture domain-specific knowledge, and a domain-agnostic LoRA module to extract transferable knowledge through contrastive acquisition and topology alignment.
COOKER performs collaborative dynamic integration of dual representations using a complementarity loss to reduce information redundancy.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors propose COOKER as a method for graph domain incremental learning.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that extensive experiments show COOKER significantly outperforms existing baselines, with up to a 4.7% improvement in average performance.

narrative_sequence.summary: GDIL seeks to learn from continuously arriving graph domains while mitigating catastrophic forgetting.
Existing prompt-based and shared-classifier low-rank adaptation approaches face adaptation or knowledge-confusion problems, while transferable knowledge is concentrated in representations.
The authors argue for domain-agnostic representations and introduce COOKER to mine inter-domain relationships.
COOKER separates domain-specific knowledge capture from transferable-knowledge extraction and integrates dual representations dynamically.
The authors report superior baseline performance, including up to a 4.7% average-performance improvement.
